audience: Repository owners and human-machine engineering teams
boundaries: This foundation does not prove Product value
Schema validation does not prove runtime behavior
The Product remains distinct from the migration Project
first_order_principles: Session memory expires with the Agent Session
Derived views do not become authority
Every connection uses an admitted Relation Kind

hypotheses.statement: A typed, evidence-bound repository model reduces semantic ambiguity enough to justify its governance cost.

intended_outcomes.statement: Current meaning, evidence, and decision state are inspectable.
Ephemeral Agents work from bounded views without owning durable memory.

problem: Repository decisions, evidence, implementations, and machine work can drift apart, leaving current meaning and authority unclear.
revision_criteria: Typed distinctions add burden without improving decisions
A simpler model preserves equivalent traceability
value_mechanism: Admitted contracts, exact Typed Relations, event-bound ontology projections, bounded Context Views, and explicit owner decisions preserve distinctions and traceability.
value_proposition: CyberAlchemy Lab keeps meaning, evidence, authority, execution, and derived views inspectable while humans and ephemeral Agents collaborate.
